title: Plug Fan Arrangement Picker
description: Nine illustrative jobs, one scored attempt each: choose plug fan Arrangement 1P, 4, 4P, 8, 8P, 9 or 9P, then see the reason, the deciding rule (drive, temperature or support) and a side-view sketch of the correct arrangement. Reference cards for all seven arrangements are available at any time.

educational.audience: Adult professional development: new application engineers, sales staff, representatives and facilities staff
learningObjectives: The learner will apply the drive, support and temperature rules for plug fan arrangements to choose the correct arrangement (1P, 4, 4P, 8, 8P, 9 or 9P) for a described job, getting at least 7 of 9 scenarios right on the first attempt.

accessibility.notes: describe() text (fallback mode); verdicts, scenario changes and the summary announced through FP.announce (aria-live); ✓/✗ glyphs and solid/dashed borders pair with colour; the deciding rule is marked with the text '◆ deciding rule' and a heavier border; keys 1-7 choose, Enter checks and goes on; every button is reachable with Tab and focus moves to the next sensible control.

controls.label: Check
controls.purpose: Check the choice (Enter); one scored attempt

controls.label: Reference cards
controls.purpose: Open or close the seven arrangement cards (exploration)

controls.label: Start over
controls.purpose: Reset all nine scenarios and the score

rules: Rule 1: drive type from the scenario (direct or belt)
Rule 2: direct drive with a hot airstream excludes 4/4P; use 8/8P

Rule 3: wall not sufficient, or a low-vibration requirement, gives the P (grade-mounted) version; otherwise wall-mounted. Belt drive on grade: motor on its own base is 1P, motor on the fan pedestal is 9P
Exactly one arrangement is correct per scenario; one scored attempt
assumptions: Scenarios are illustrative jobs written for Chapter 6
limitations: The side-view sketches are schematic, not to scale; sizes and limits come from the current catalog

sources: Source: FanPedia pp. 171-172 (Technical Descriptions, plug Arrangements 4, 4P, 8, 8P, 9, 9P) and p. 14 (belt-driven plug fan, Arr. 9P)

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit a choice before the answer is shown, then tie the answer to the deciding rule
keyQuestions: Is the job direct drive or belt drive?
Does a hot airstream rule out the impeller on the motor shaft?
Can the wall carry the fan, and is there a low-vibration requirement?
commonMisconceptions: Arrangement 4 is always best because it has the fewest parts, even with a hot airstream
The P versions are a different fan rather than the same arrangement mounted to grade
Every grade-mounted belt-driven fan is 9P (1P has the motor on its own base)
assessmentOpportunities: Running score shown as 'Scenarios correct: n of 9'; mastery is 7 of 9 on the first attempt.
